title: Base change for an arbitrary morphism, against an open immersion
statement:
Fix the finite coefficient $A=A_{E,n}$ and the geometric data of [def-weil-ambient-exceptional-adjoint]. Let $f:X\to Y$ be separated of finite type carrying that ambient exceptional right adjoint datum, and let $g:Y'\hookrightarrow Y$ be an open immersion [def-weil-open-immersion]. Form the Cartesian square [def-weil-pbc-cartesian-square], with $X'=X\times_Y Y'$, $g':X'\to X$, and $f':X'\to Y'$. On the ordinary derived categories of pro-etale $A$-module sheaves [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site], the canonical exceptional base-change comparison
$$
\beta_f: Lg'^*Rf^\times\longrightarrow Rf'^\times Lg^*
$$
is an isomorphism. Here the adjoint for $f'$ is obtained using the base-changed compactification and the restricted FullCD bound. In particular this applies when $Y'$ is an affine open of $Y$.

Independently of the ambient datum, let $f:X\to Y$ be any separated finite-type morphism of finite-type $k$-schemes, $k=\overline{\mathbf F}_q$, let $g:Y'\hookrightarrow Y$ be an open immersion, and form the Cartesian square as above. For the finite coefficients of [def-sf-fullcd-used-class], use the constructible exceptional inverse image $Rf^!$ of [def-weil-exceptional-inverse-image], interpreted by [cor-sf-ambient-adjoint-discharge]. For every coefficient sheaf $K$ of the etale-origin class [def-sf-fullcd-used-class], regarded as a complex in degree zero, and also for every bounded constructible $K$ on $Y$ [def-weil-finite-torsion-constructibility], the canonical comparison
$$
Lg'^*Rf^!K\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }Rf'^!Lg^*K
$$
is an isomorphism. This clause uses the relative adjunction on bounded-below complexes of etale origin; it does not assert the unrestricted ambient datum. It is this bounded-class comparison that affine-chart assembly consumes.

proof.text: The datum of [def-weil-ambient-exceptional-adjoint] already contains a compactification $X\xrightarrow{j_0}\overline X\xrightarrow{p}Y$ and an integer $c$ with $\operatorname{FullCD}(p,A;c)$. Use that compactification, rather than invoking Nagata over a base not assumed qcqs. The factorization $\overline X\xrightarrow{\mathrm{id}}\overline X\xrightarrow{p}Y$ compactifies $p$, so [lem-sp-fullcd-ambient-adjoint] supplies its ambient adjunction with the required comparison coherence. This verifies the ambient-datum hypothesis needed when applying the proper case.For the application to $p$, its source is finite type over $S$: properness gives finite type over $Y$, and composing the finite lists of affine algebra generators with those for $Y\to S$ gives finite type over $S$. Thus the scheme-base hypotheses of the existence input hold as well.

source.place: Proof, first sentence; sk-prop-sf-existence(b) for the missing adjunction hypothesis

proof.text: Pull back the compactification along $g$, putting $\overline X'=\overline X\times_Y Y'$, $\overline g:\overline X'\to\overline X$, $j_0':X'\to\overline X'$ and $p':\overline X'\to Y'$. Open immersions remain open by [lem-weil-pbc-open-immersion-base-change], and $p'$ remains proper by [lem-weil-pbc-proper-base-change]. Thus this is a compactification of $f'$; the equality $p'j_0'=f'$ follows by composing the two projections to $Y$ and $Y'$ in the fibre-product universal property. No assertion that $g$ is quasi-compact is needed. The schemes $X'$ and $\overline X'$ are finite type over the new base $Y'$ because finite lists of affine algebra generators and finite affine covers pull back by tensor product; separatedness pulls back by [lem-weil-pbc-separated-base-change]. Thus the ambient datum for the base-changed maps is read with base scheme $Y'$ rather than requiring $Y'$ finite type over the original $S$. The invertibility of $\ell$ is inherited from $S$ along the structure maps and the open inclusion.

source.place: Proof, compactification and its base change, expanded

proof.text: The FullCD bound restricts to $p'$. For a sheaf $F'$ on $\overline X'_{\mathrm{proet}}$, set $F=\overline g_!F'$ using [def-weil-extension-by-zero]. Restricted back to $\overline X'$, this is $F'$: the defining presheaf on every object over this open is exactly $F'$, and its covers are covers in the localized site. Apply the relative vanishing clause of [def-weil-full-cohomological-dimension] first to the open object $Y'\to Y$, and then to each object $V\to Y'$ regarded as an object over $Y$; localization of the weakly-etale site is [lem-weil-proetale-weakly-etale-localization]. Under $\overline X\times_YV=\overline X'\times_{Y'}V$, the restricted sheaf is exactly the pullback of $F'$. This proves both clauses of $\operatorname{FullCD}(p',A;c)$, for every $F'$. Apply [lem-sp-fullcd-ambient-adjoint] to the base-changed compactification of $f'$ and the identity-open compactification of $p'$ to obtain their ambient adjoints and coherent units/counits.

source.place: Proof, justification that the proper-case and reduction adjoints exist after open base change

proof.text: Give the closed subset $Y\setminus Y'$ its reduced induced closed subscheme structure using [lem-weil-pbc-reduced-induced-closed-subscheme]. Apply [prop-exc-base-change-proper] to $p$ and the given open immersion $g$. Steps 1-3 supply the adjunction data for $p,p'$ and their compactifications. Its conclusion is precisely the invertibility of $\beta_p:L\overline g^*Rp^\times\to R(p')^\times Lg^*$. The hypothesis of [cor-exc-base-change-reduces-to-proper] is therefore satisfied for the chosen compactification of $f$. That corollary states directly that invertibility of this canonical comparison for the proper part implies invertibility of the canonical comparison $\beta_f:Lg'^*Rf^\times\to Rf'^\times Lg^*$. Apply that implication to obtain the required comparison isomorphism for $f$.Only the first, conditional assertion of [prop-exc-base-change-proper] is used here. Its subsequent coefficient-class discharge sentence supplies no hypothesis or conclusion to this step; the independent coefficient-class argument is Steps 5-7.

For the independent coefficient-class clause, first choose a compactification without an ambient datum. The field $k$ is Noetherian because its only ideals are $0$ and $k$. Hence [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian] makes $Y$ Noetherian, and [lem-weil-pbc-locally-noetherian-quasi-separated] makes it quasi-separated. For every affine open $U\subseteq Y$, both $U$ and $U\cap Y'$ are Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-open-subscheme-noetherian], so $g$ is quasi-compact; [lem-weil-pbc-qc-open-immersion-finite-type] then makes $g$ finite type, and finite-type composition makes $Y'$ finite type over $k$. Thus [thm-nagata-compactification] supplies $X\xrightarrow{j_0}\overline X\xrightarrow pY$. Properness and finite type give $\overline X$ finite type over $k$; [lem-kun-dimension-finite-type] supplies a bound $d\ge0$. Pull back this compactification; [lem-weil-pbc-open-immersion-base-change], [lem-weil-pbc-proper-base-change] and [def-pc-fibre-product] give $j_0',p'$ and $f'=p'j_0'$, and the finite-type calculation of Step 2 applies to the base-changed schemes. The proper schemes $\overline X,\overline X'$ and the original schemes are Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian]; the Noetherian-open argument also applies to $g'$ and $\overline g$, so all these open maps are finite type. Both proper parts are quasi-compact and quasi-separated by their finite-type and separated definitions. A finite dimension bound for each pulled-back compactification follows from [lem-kun-dimension-finite-type] as well. These facts allow [thm-sf-ambient-adjoint-class] to be used for $f,f'$ without assuming any ambient datum.

source.place: Independent coefficient-class clause: verify the Noetherian and compactification hypotheses of sk-prop-sf-existence(c).

proof.text:
Work in the full bounded-below etale-origin categories $\mathcal C_T=\mathcal D^+_{\mathrm{et}}(T,A)$ of [def-sf-etale-origin-subcategory]. Construct the proper/open interchange on this class, rather than applying an ambient-adjoint theorem to relative functors. For the proper/open square with vertical maps $p',p$ and horizontal opens $\overline g,g$, [lem-cbc-proper-open-interchange-coherence] supplies the specific etale isomorphism
$$\Gamma^e:g_!^eRp'_{e,*}\xrightarrow{\sim}Rp_{e,*}\overline g_!^e.$$
Write $s_p:\nu_Y^*Rp_{e,*}\xrightarrow{\sim}Rp_*\nu_{\overline X}^*$ and $s_{p'}$ for [prop-weil-pbc-comparison-direct-image], and $e_g:\nu_Y^*g_!^e\xrightarrow{\sim}g_!\nu_{Y'}^*$ and $e_{\overline g}$ for [lem-cbc-proetale-extension-zero-comparison]. Exactness of the two extension-by-zero functors and comparison pullback, [lem-weil-extension-by-zero-exact], [lem-sf-comparison-pullback-exact] and [lem-sf-exact-functor-derived-triangulated], makes the sheaf comparisons into termwise derived comparisons. For $N=\nu_{\overline X'}^*H$, define $\Gamma^p_N:g_!Rp'_*N\to Rp_*\overline g_!N$ by the five arrows
$$
g_!Rp'_*\nu^*H
\xrightarrow{g_!s_{p'}^{-1}}g_!\nu^*Rp'_{e,*}H
\xrightarrow{e_g^{-1}}\nu^*g_!^eRp'_{e,*}H
\xrightarrow{\nu^*\Gamma^e}\nu^*Rp_{e,*}\overline g_!^eH
\xrightarrow{s_p}Rp_*\nu^*\overline g_!^eH
\xrightarrow{Rp_*e_{\overline g}}Rp_*\overline g_!\nu^*H.
$$
Each arrow is an isomorphism. Full faithfulness [thm-weil-pbc-site-comparison] extends this construction to every morphism between witnessed objects, by conjugating with the witnesses; a change of witness conjugates by the unique corresponding etale isomorphism, so gives the identical map on $N$. The two open composites $j_0g'=\overline g j_0'$ give
$$j_{0!}g'_!\cong\overline g_!j'_{0!}:$$
indeed, successively using [prop-exc-open-adjoint] identifies both Hom sets into any $M$ with $\operatorname{Hom}(-,g'^*j_0^*M)=\operatorname{Hom}(-,j_0'^*\overline g^*M)$, and [lem-galois-yoneda-fully-faithful] identifies the left adjoints. Thus the canonical proper/open support comparison for $f$ is the isomorphism
$$\Theta: Rf_!g'_!=Rp_*j_{0!}g'_!\xrightarrow{\sim}Rp_*\overline g_!j'_{0!}\xrightarrow{(\Gamma^p)^{-1}}g_!Rp'_*j'_{0!}=g_!Rf'_!.$$
Its inputs and outputs are bounded-below of etale origin: extension by zero preserves this class by its displayed comparison with the etale functor, and compact support preserves it by [lem-sf-class-compact-support-comparison]. This constructs the proper comparison first and then pastes the open part, as in the source, but entirely on the relative class. The pasting, identity and base-change equations of $\Gamma^e$, and the identity/composition compatibility of $s_p,e_g$, ensure that $\Theta$ uses the specified canonical support maps, not an arbitrary isomorphism of its endpoints.

proof.text:
Put $F=Rf_!$, $F'=Rf'_!$, $G=Rf^!$, $G'=Rf'^!$, using [def-weil-exceptional-inverse-image] and the relative Hom bijections of [thm-sf-ambient-adjoint-class](2). On the class of Step 6, $g'^*G L$ and $G'g^*L$ belong to $\mathcal C_{X'}$. For $G,G'$ this follows from their formula $\nu^*f^\times R\nu_*$; restriction along an open also preserves etale origin. Explicitly, [lem-cbc-comparison-pullback-sections] evaluates $\nu_X^*H$ at $W\to X'$ as $\Gamma(W_{\mathrm{et}},H|_W)$, exactly the value of $\nu_{X'}^*(H|_{X'})$; the isomorphism preserves every module operation by naturality. Localization [lem-weil-proetale-weakly-etale-localization] identifies this with $g'^*$, and exact comparison pullback [lem-sf-comparison-pullback-exact], together with exact constant-coefficient inverse image [prop-weil-pbc-proetale-constant-exact], makes the equality valid termwise on bounded-below complexes. All pullbacks in this proof therefore agree with their derived pullbacks. This reasoning applies to $g$ too.

For every $M\in\mathcal C_{X'}$ and the stated input $L$, the following five bijections are natural in $M,L$:
$$
\operatorname{Hom}(M,g'^*G L)
\cong\operatorname{Hom}(g'_!M,G L)
\cong\operatorname{Hom}(Fg'_!M,L)
\xrightarrow{\ t\mapsto t\Theta_M^{-1}\ }\operatorname{Hom}(g_!F'M,L)
\cong\operatorname{Hom}(F'M,g^*L)
\cong\operatorname{Hom}(M,G'g^*L).
$$
The first and fourth are [prop-exc-open-adjoint]; the second and fifth are exactly the relative adjunctions of [thm-sf-ambient-adjoint-class]. Their hypotheses hold because Step 6 supplies etale origin and boundedness below for $g'_!M,F'M$. Let $\eta_g$ be the unit of $g_!\dashv g^*$ and $\varepsilon_{g'}$ the counit of $g'_!\dashv g'^*$. To identify the map, not just its endpoints, form the reverse support comparison
$$\delta_F:F'g'^*\xrightarrow{\eta_g}g^*g_!F'g'^*\xrightarrow{g^*\Theta^{-1}}g^*Fg'_!g'^*\xrightarrow{g^*F\varepsilon_{g'}}g^*F.$$
Successive transposition in the displayed Hom chain sends $u:M\to g'^*G L$ to $\beta_Lu$, where
$$\beta:g'^*G\xrightarrow{\eta_{F'}}G'F'g'^*G\xrightarrow{G'\delta_FG}G'g^*FG\xrightarrow{G'g^*\varepsilon_F}G'g^*.$$
This is precisely the canonical relative exceptional comparison: it is the mate [def-weil-pbc-adjunction-mate] of the reverse support comparison obtained by the proper square and its open paste in Step 6. The formulas fix all units, counits and orientations. The Hom chain is bijective for every $M$ in the full class containing both endpoints; [lem-galois-yoneda-fully-faithful] therefore makes $\beta_L$ an isomorphism. It applies to every degree-zero etale-origin sheaf, including infinite ones, and to every bounded constructible complex: the latter has an etale-origin witness as stated in [def-weil-exceptional-inverse-image]. All five bijections hold for the entire bounded-below complex; thus no extension of a sheaf-only comparison, no shift-compatibility assertion inferred from naturality alone, and no truncation lemma is required. Compactification coherence is that of [thm-sf-ambient-adjoint-class](3) and the canonical support comparisons in Step 6. Affine-open inclusions give the stated specialization.Explicitly, in the full class put $B=g'^*GL$ and $C=G'g^*L$. Surjectivity of $\operatorname{Hom}(C,B)\to\operatorname{Hom}(C,C)$ gives $v:C\to B$ with $\beta_Lv=\mathrm{id}_C$. Injectivity on $\operatorname{Hom}(B,B)$, applied to $v\beta_L$ and $\mathrm{id}_B$, gives $v\beta_L=\mathrm{id}_B$. This is the required inverse to the specified comparison.
